facility_roles.quote: The CANGAROO-III imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope system which consists of four telescopes are operated in Woomera

intervals.label: CANGAROO operations
intervals.note: Start: the 3.8 m CANGAROO-I telescope began in 1992. End: the activities in Australia were stopped in 2011 (arXiv:1207.6003).
intervals.quote: It started from a 3.8-m telescope[1] (CANGAROO-I) in 1992.

intervals.label: CANGAROO-I (3.8 m telescope)
intervals.quote: operated from 1992 to 1998 near Woomera, South Australia

intervals.label: CANGAROO-II (10 m mount, 7 m mirror)
intervals.note: The mirror was extended to 10 m in 2000, and this telescope became the first CANGAROO-III telescope (T1).
intervals.quote: The second stage, CANGAROO- II, commenced in 1999 with the construction of a 10 m telescope mount with a mirror initially of 7 m diameter. The mirror was extended to 10 m in 2000

intervals.label: CANGAROO-III (10 m telescopes)
intervals.note: March 2000 is the first 10 m telescope. The stereoscopic array of four was planned to be complete in 2004 (arXiv:astro-ph/0106346, a plan, not a report); four telescopes were operating by the 2006 outburst paper (arXiv:0712.3094). End from the 2011 stop of activities.
intervals.quote: The first telescope of this array is the upgraded version of the CANGAROO-II 7 m telescope and has been in operation since March 2000.

intervals.label: observing activities ended
intervals.note: A 2024 review says the array terminated its operation a few years after H.E.S.S. began (arXiv:2406.15037); the 2011 date is from arXiv:1207.6003 alone.
intervals.quote: Eventually, the activities in Australia were stopped in 2011.

name: CANGAROO
notes: Disputed early results: the collaboration's own 2009 reanalysis of the 3.8 m telescope data (arXiv:0906.4924) found no significant TeV signal from compact regions around PSR B1706-44 or in the northeast rim of SN 1006, in response to H.E.S.S. results; the Mirzoyan review (arXiv:2406.15037) says H.E.S.S. could not confirm some CANGAROO results. See the log for the exact wording.
The first CANGAROO-III telescope (T1) was not in use by 2007-2009 (arXiv:0908.1610); analyses used T2-T4.
No INSPIRE experiment id is recorded: INSPIRE was not contacted by this stream.

summary.plain: Gamma-ray telescopes in the South Australian outback run by Japanese and Australian universities from 1992 to 2011, growing from one 3.8 metre mirror to an array of four 10 metre telescopes.
summary.technical: CANGAROO imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes at Woomera: the 3.8 m CANGAROO-I (1992-1998), the CANGAROO-II 7 m then 10 m telescope (1999-2000) and the four-telescope 10 m CANGAROO-III array (first telescope March 2000). Activities stopped in 2011.

unique_capabilities.quote: The four 10 m diameter telescopes can operate independently or as an array.
unique_capabilities.value: Four 10 m imaging telescopes that can operate independently or as a stereoscopic array, for sub-TeV gamma-ray astronomy.
